answer: Escrowed Action Histories: each identity's past actions form a public chain; new identities must replay a random sample of a verified member's history before transacting. Sampling from a garden of logged actions grows linearly, so an attacker farming many fresh identities pays full replay effort per identity. A comet of recent activity flags outliers for heavier sampling, and any identity sitting on an isolated knoll of self-referential history is charged extra verification until it links to the main graph. The per-identity cost is the compute to reproduce sampled proofs, not a fee.
